steps.title: Two pawns against one
steps.source: I shall now give a couple of simple endings of two Pawns against one, or three against two, that the reader may see how they can be won. […] It is up to the student to work things out for himself.

narration.say: White has two pawns, Black has one. It looks easy.
But the obvious move does not win. Let us see why first.

steps.title: The tempting push
steps.source: In this position White cannot win by playing 1 P - B 6, because Black plays, not P x P, which would lose, but 1…K - Kt 1, and if then 2 P x P, K x P, and draws.

narration.say: But Black does not take. He plays king to g8.
If White now takes on g7, the black king takes back, and it is a draw.
Back to the start. White wins, but with the king first. Your move.

exercise.prompt: White to move and win. Start with the king.

feedback.f6: That is the tempting push: Black answers Kg8 and draws.
feedback.Ke5: Backwards. The king should go forward, towards e7.
feedback.*: The king heads for e7, next to the pawns and the black king.

exercise.hint: The king goes round, via d7.

narration.say: King to e7. Black to h8.
Now f6 works, because the white king protects f7 and f8.
If Black does not take, f7 and the pawn queens with mate. So Black takes.
The black king is in the corner. Your king can lock him in.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Keep the black king in the corner.

feedback.g7: Check, but after Kxg7 White has nothing left. First lock the king in.
feedback.Kxf6: Kxf6 takes a pawn, but then the black king gets out of the corner.
feedback.*: The king steps next to the g-pawn and takes g7 and g8 away.

exercise.success: 4. Kf7. Black can only move his pawn: f5.

steps.title: Promote and mate
steps.source: 4 K - B 7, P - B 4; 5 P - Kt 7 ch, K - R 2; 6 P - Kt 8 (Q) ch, K - R 3; 7 Q - Kt 6 mate.

narration.say: Pawn to g7, check. Black to h7.
The pawn becomes a queen, with check. Black to h6.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.

feedback.*: Not mate. The queen can land next to the black king, protected by your own king.

exercise.success: Checkmate. The king did the work; the pawns only moved when it was safe.

narration.say: The obvious pawn push can throw away the win.
Bring the king up first, so that the pawns can advance under its protection.
